newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian police smash T-shirt smuggling gang.
newsitem.headline: Italian police smash T-shirt smuggling gang.

text.p: Police in Italy said on Thursday they had seized two million illegally imported T-shirts and were investigating 24 people after a two-year operation into textiles smuggling.
Finance police in Milan said the T-shirts were worth 20 billion lire ($13 million).
The scam had avoided customs duties of two billion lire ($1.32 million) and distorted the textile market by dodging European Union import quotas, a statement said.
Police became aware of the smuggling ring in July 1994 when they intercepted a truck bringing a consignment of Chinese-made T-shirts to an illegal warehouse in Milan.
"The smugglers were using the Marco Polo route not to import drugs, silver or cigarettes but textiles," the statement said.
It said the operation was run by an Italian family living in Switzerland and had printed its own illegal custom documents to avoid duties.
Four members of the family were among the 24 people under investigation, the statement said.
Eleven people faced charges of fiscal fraud, smuggling and receiving stolen goods and a further 13 were suspected of smuggling and aiding and abetting the operation, it said.
